# datadog_github_oidc_persona_mapping (Resource)

Provides a GitHub Actions OIDC persona mapping for Datadog workload identity federation. The mapping allows a GitHub Actions workload whose OIDC token matches the `claim_matchers` patterns to authenticate as the Datadog user or service account identified by `account_identifier`. The identity creating the mapping must have every permission assigned to the target identity. Creating the initial mapping requires API and application credentials with the Workload Identity Federation write permission; a provider already using federation cannot bootstrap its own mapping. Mappings cannot be updated; changing any attribute replaces the mapping. This resource uses a public beta API and is subject to change.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "datadog_role" "read_only" {
  filter = "Datadog Read Only Role"
}

resource "datadog_service_account" "terraform" {
  email = "terraform-service-account@example.com"
  name  = "Terraform service account"
  roles = [data.datadog_role.read_only.id]
}

resource "datadog_github_oidc_persona_mapping" "terraform" {
  # A service account's handle is its UUID, so `id` is both stable and already the
  # canonical value Datadog stores. Using `email` here would work, but Datadog
  # normalizes it to the handle, leaving this attribute import-unstable.
  account_identifier = datadog_service_account.terraform.id
  claim_matchers = {
    # The owner in the `sub` prefix must be a literal, not a regex. Replace
    # my-org/terraform with a repository you control: the mapping grants the
    # mapped identity's Datadog access to every workflow that can mint a
    # matching OIDC token, so never configure a repository you do not own.
    sub        = "repo:my-org/terraform:ref:refs/heads/main"
    repository = "^my-org/terraform$"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `account_identifier` (String) The email or handle of the Datadog user or service account that the GitHub workload authenticates as. For a Terraform-managed service account, prefer the stable UUID exported by `datadog_service_account.id`; Datadog accepts it as the service account identifier. Datadog normalizes an email to the account's handle, so the handle form is the only value that survives `terraform import` unchanged — importing a mapping configured by email produces a diff on this attribute, which forces replacement. String length must be at least 1.
- `claim_matchers` (Attributes) GitHub Actions OIDC claims to match against. Each attribute is a regular expression; `sub` is required and all other claims are optional. A token matches only when all provided patterns match simultaneously (AND semantics). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--claim_matchers))

### Read-Only

- `account_uuid` (String) The UUID of the Datadog user or service account resolved from `account_identifier`.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

<a id="nestedatt--claim_matchers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `claim_matchers`

Required:

- `sub` (String) Regular expression matched against the required `sub` claim of the GitHub Actions OIDC token. It must start with the literal `repo:<OWNER>/` prefix; the owner cannot be a regex. String length must be at least 1.

Optional:

- `actor` (String) Regular expression matched against the `actor` claim of the GitHub Actions OIDC token. String length must be at least 1.
- `actor_id` (String) Regular expression matched against the `actor_id` claim of the GitHub Actions OIDC token. String length must be at least 1.
- `enterprise` (String) Regular expression matched against the `enterprise` claim of the GitHub Actions OIDC token. String length must be at least 1.
- `enterprise_id` (String) Regular expression matched against the `enterprise_id` claim of the GitHub Actions OIDC token. String length must be at least 1.
- `environment` (String) Regular expression matched against the `environment` claim of the GitHub Actions OIDC token. String length must be at least 1.
- `event_name` (String) Regular expression matched against the `event_name` claim of the GitHub Actions OIDC token. String length must be at least 1.
- `job_workflow_ref` (String) Regular expression matched against the `job_workflow_ref` claim of the GitHub Actions OIDC token. String length must be at least 1.
- `ref` (String) Regular expression matched against the `ref` claim of the GitHub Actions OIDC token. String length must be at least 1.
- `ref_type` (String) Regular expression matched against the `ref_type` claim of the GitHub Actions OIDC token. String length must be at least 1.
- `repository` (String) Regular expression matched against the `repository` claim of the GitHub Actions OIDC token. String length must be at least 1.
- `repository_id` (String) Regular expression matched against the `repository_id` claim of the GitHub Actions OIDC token. String length must be at least 1.
- `repository_owner` (String) Regular expression matched against the `repository_owner` claim of the GitHub Actions OIDC token. String length must be at least 1.
- `repository_owner_id` (String) Regular expression matched against the `repository_owner_id` claim of the GitHub Actions OIDC token. String length must be at least 1.
- `repository_visibility` (String) Regular expression matched against the `repository_visibility` claim of the GitHub Actions OIDC token. String length must be at least 1.
- `runner_environment` (String) Regular expression matched against the `runner_environment` claim of the GitHub Actions OIDC token. String length must be at least 1.
- `workflow` (String) Regular expression matched against the `workflow` claim of the GitHub Actions OIDC token. String length must be at least 1.
- `workflow_ref` (String) Regular expression matched against the `workflow_ref` claim of the GitHub Actions OIDC token. String length must be at least 1.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import datadog_github_oidc_persona_mapping.terraform "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
```
